title: Prescriptive analysis: what to do about it

videos.script: A forecast tells you what is likely. It does not tell you what to do. {{gap}} That is the last of the four kinds of analysis, and the one closest to a decision. {{shape}} A prescriptive question has three parts: the options, the limits on them, and what you are trying to achieve. {{reorder}} First, the smallest prescriptive tool there is. A reorder rule for garden-hose reels at Varanda's warehouse, built in a sheet. Then the supplier slows down, and you see what a rule nobody updates costs. {{options}} Next, three options for a December promotion. The one that sells the most earns the least. You work out how many sets each discount would need to sell to break even. {{decide}} Last, who acts on the answer. Some decisions should run by themselves. Others belong to a person, in a meeting. The difference is what a mistake costs, and whether it can be undone.
